walkthroughs.body_html:
Problem Solving With Programming — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Problem Solving With Programming brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Problem Solving With Programming.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is a high-level programming language?
options: Assembly
Machine code
Python
Binary
Internet Data Engine
Integrated Development Environment
Internal Debugging Editor
Interpreted Dynamic Executable

mcqs.q: What is the difference between OR and XOR?
options: To make the function run faster.
OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
OR is true when at least one input is true; XOR is true when exactly one input is true.
They are the same gate with different names.

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
The first one added (FIFO).
Any item, randomly.
The most recently added (top) - LIFO.

mcqs.q: Why must a recursive function have a base case?
options: Any item, randomly.
To make the function run faster.
Because the syntax requires it.
Without it, the function calls itself indefinitely, causing a stack overflow.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Semantics”?
options: Programming language close to human language (Python, Java) that must be translated to machine code.
Integrated Development Environment: editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger and tools combined in one application.
Meaning of a syntactically valid program - what the code actually does when executed.
Non-executing text in source code that explains the program to human readers.

Assembly or machine code, closer to hardware, providing direct control of the processor.

Integrated Development Environment: editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger and tools combined in one application.
